Control run of the same script against Alpine's musl Chromium 136
(`SPIKE_BROWSER=chromium CHROMIUM_PATH=/usr/bin/chromium`): every probe above
passes except `page.keyboard.type` after `page.click('#inp')` (a Chromium-136 +
Playwright-1.62 click-on-input timing quirk; `focus()` + `keyboard.type` works
there too). The failures in the table are therefore Obscura gaps, not harness
problems.

## Failure notes

| Probe | What actually happens |
| --- | --- |
| `page.mouse` move-while-pressed | Playwright 1.62 calls `Input.setInterceptDrags` as soon as the mouse moves with a button held; Obscura answers `Unknown Input method`, and the move rejects. `mouse.move` before `mouse.down`, `click({ force: true })` and `hover` do not hit this path and work. |
| Pointer events | Neither Playwright's mouse nor raw `Input.dispatchMouseEvent` produce `pointerdown/pointermove/pointerup`; only `mousedown/mouseup/click` fire (no `mousemove` at all). `PointerEvent` exists but a constructed event has `clientX`, `pointerId` and `buttons` undefined, and `Element.setPointerCapture` / `hasPointerCapture` are undefined. |
| `page.keyboard.type` (after `click`) | The click-to-focus step does not focus the input, so typed text goes nowhere. `page.focus()` + `keyboard.type`/`press` works, and raw `Input.dispatchKeyEvent` works. `Input.insertText` is unsupported. |
| `locator.fill` | Hangs (the fill path uses `Input.insertText` and selection APIs). |
| `page.setContent` | Hangs waiting for the load lifecycle of the rewritten document; `page.goto` to a served URL works. |
| `locator.click` (non-force) | Hangs in Playwright's actionability/hit-target checks; `click({ force: true })` completes and dispatches mouse events. |

Everything Playwright needs for viewport control works: `Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride`
(what `page.setViewportSize` and `newContext({ viewport })` send) and
`Browser.getWindowForTarget` both succeed and `innerWidth/innerHeight` follow.

## What this means for the Gridla suites

Gridla's interaction layer (`packages/gridla/src/react/interaction.ts`) is
pointer-event driven: drags and resizes start on `pointerdown`, call
`setPointerCapture(event.pointerId)`, track `pointermove`, and end on
`pointerup`. The e2e fixtures (`tests/e2e/fixtures.ts` `dragBy`/`resizeBy`)
drive that with `page.mouse.move/down/up`. On Obscura v0.2.1:

- No pointer events are ever delivered (neither from Playwright's `page.mouse`
  nor from raw CDP `Input.dispatchMouseEvent`), `PointerEvent` init dictionaries
  are ignored, and `setPointerCapture` does not exist. Every drag, resize,
  proximity-handle and pointer-capture scenario is untestable, regardless of how
  the input is injected. Synthesising pointer events from `page.evaluate` is
  also out, because the constructed events carry no coordinates.
- `page.mouse.move` while a button is held fails outright on
  `Input.setInterceptDrags`, so the current `dragBy` helper cannot even reach
  the engine.
- Rendering/layout probes that Gridla's non-interactive assertions rely on all
  pass: static page load, ES modules, `evaluate`, `getBoundingClientRect`
  (including CSS `transform`), `ResizeObserver`, `requestAnimationFrame`,
  `matchMedia`, `localStorage`, screenshots, viewport sizing, isolated contexts.

Conclusion: Obscura is viable only as a **layout/projection smoke lane** (load
a demo, assert item rects, responsive re-projection via `setViewportSize`,
screenshots), not as a substitute for the Chromium/Firefox/WebKit gate. All
pointer-interaction specs must be excluded from it.

## Runtime notes

- Run the spike and the Obscura lane under **Node**, not Bun: Playwright's
  bundled `ws` client never completes the CDP WebSocket handshake with Obscura
  under Bun 1.3.x (a raw Bun `WebSocket` to the same endpoint works, and Node
  connects immediately). `bunx playwright test` already executes the runner
  under Node.
- `obscura serve` must be started with `--allow-private-network` or it refuses
  to load pages from `127.0.0.1`.
- The existing `obscura` project in `playwright.config.ts` passes
  `connectOptions.wsEndpoint`, which makes Playwright use its own `connect`
  protocol; Obscura only speaks CDP, so that project can never attach. It needs
  a fixture that calls `chromium.connectOverCDP` instead (see PIN.md and the
  recommendation in the spike report).
